value: Nearly all synbiotics in published trials or on the market are of the complementary form.
quote: To our knowledge, nearly all synbiotics used in published clinical trials or available commercially are of the complementary form 15 , irrespective of whether they have been deliberately designed or named as such.

value: Example 1 (XOS with B. lactis Bi-07) meets the definition of a complementary synbiotic.
quote: Taken together, this tested product meets our definition of a complementary synbiotic.

value: Example 1 does not meet the definition of a synergistic synbiotic, since Bifidobacterium did not increase with the combination.
quote: However, because an increase of Bifidobacterium was not observed in individuals fed the combination product, it does not meet our definition of a synergistic synbiotic.

value: Example 2 (GOS with B. adolescentis IVS-1) did not support the definition of a synergistic synbiotic, though all arms improved permeability markers.
quote: Although the combination, probiotic and prebiotic arms all improved the markers of colonic permeability and all increased faecal bifidobacteria levels, the study did not support our definition of a synergistic synbiotic.

value: In one RCT of 225 adults, B. lactis 420 with polydextrose reduced body fat mass by 4.5% while each alone had no effect.
quote: In one RCT 46 of 225 adults with overweight and obesity, a combination of Bifidobacterium animalis subsp. lactis 420 and polydextrose (12 g per day) resulted in a relative reduction in body fat mass of 4.5%, whereas the individual treatments had no effect.

value: That RCT alone does not show the combination was a complementary or synergistic synbiotic, as selective utilization was not established.
quote: Thus, by itself, this study does not provide sufficient evidence that the tested combination was either a complementary or a synergistic synbiotic.

value: No safety-related data were reported in 37% of RCTs in a review of 384 interventions.
